title: Zelensky signs law lowering Ukraine's minimum mobilisation age from 27 to 25
body:
On 2 April 2024, President Volodymyr Zelensky signed three laws on mobilisation, according to the Kyiv Independent, which cited the website of Ukraine's parliament. Under the changes, men aged 25 and older became eligible for compulsory military service, down from 27. Parliament had approved the age change in May 2023. Men aged 18 to 25 with prior military experience can also be mobilised.

The laws also created a digital register for conscripts. The government said it would speed up the collection and use of military records and give people online documents confirming their military registration status. The "partially eligible" medical status was abolished, so that medical reports list only "eligible" or "non-eligible", and anyone previously rated partially eligible must be re-examined.

Other provisions allow conscripts to undergo 12 months of treatment without a mandatory medical examination, to be exempted from service to care for sick children under 14, and to take leave after childbirth or after being wounded. The government said the changes were meant to increase the number of available troops in 2024. A broader mobilisation bill had been withdrawn and was still under parliamentary review at the time. It was signed separately in mid-April 2024, according to Al Jazeera, and added duties to update draft data and new punishments for draft evasion.
